name: FreeBSD iflib network driver
description: Destination-OS profile for porting a Linux netdev driver to a FreeBSD iflib driver. Declares (a) which Linux-only source surfaces must be removed before the per-method porting loop, and (b) the target-mandated work items that have no Linux counterpart and must therefore be created rather than translated.

exclusion._comment: Rules are evaluated in order; the first match decides. keep_overrides are evaluated before every rule and always win. disposition: drop = out of scope for this target, no replacement; replace = the Linux mechanism is superseded by the listed target work items; defer = valid on the target but out of scope for the initial port.

keep_overrides.reason: The virtchnl control queue is transport-independent and is required by every target work item that talks to the device.
Register maps, descriptor layouts and virtchnl message definitions are hardware contracts, not OS surfaces.

rules.rationale: Linux kernel-version compatibility shims. They exist to paper over differences between Linux releases and carry no semantics to port.
Generated Linux module glue. The target equivalent is written from scratch as TGT-MOD-001.
devlink is a Linux netlink subsystem. FreeBSD exposes the same class of device configuration and health information through the sysctl tree.
Inter-driver communication over the Linux auxiliary bus (RDMA peer driver). FreeBSD has no auxiliary bus and RDMA peering is out of scope for the initial port.
XDP and AF_XDP zero-copy sockets have no FreeBSD equivalent; iflib has no XDP hook.
VFIO mediated-device / Scalable IOV assignable device interfaces are Linux VFIO constructs. FreeBSD PCI passthrough uses a different model and is out of scope.
ethtool is a Linux ioctl ABI. Its responsibilities split across the FreeBSD media layer, interface capabilities, counters and the sysctl tree.
Every Linux-specific construct in the function belongs to an XDP/zero-copy family with no target counterpart.
Every Linux-specific construct in the function belongs to the auxiliary bus family, which does not exist on the target.
The function exists only to expose state through sysfs/procfs/debugfs. On the target this surface is the sysctl tree.
The function belongs exclusively to subsystems that are out of scope for the initial iflib port.

workflows.title: Device attach and iflib context bring-up

work_items.title: Kernel module declaration and load/unload lifecycle
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: module_init/module_exit, MODULE_* macros, pci_register_driver
obligations: Declare the driver with DRIVER_MODULE against the pci bus and a device_method_t table.
Declare MODULE_DEPEND on pci and iflib, and MODULE_VERSION.
Handle MOD_LOAD/MOD_UNLOAD/MOD_QUIESCE, refusing unload while interfaces are attached.
Never execute device work from the module event handler.
acceptance_criteria: kldload followed by kldunload completes without a leaked reference or panic.
Repeated load/unload cycles leave no allocated memory or busdma tags behind.

work_items.title: PCI probe and device identification table
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: struct pci_device_id table and pci_driver.probe
obligations: Express the supported device list as a pci_vendor_info_t array referenced from the shared context.
Return the correct BUS_PROBE_* precedence and set the device description.
Match the device identifier set of the source driver exactly; do not silently widen or narrow it.
acceptance_criteria: Every device identifier supported by the source driver is present in the target table.
Probe attaches on supported hardware and declines on unrelated devices.

work_items.title: Shared context (if_shared_ctx_t) definition
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: implicit netdev/driver constants spread across the Linux probe path
obligations: Derive every descriptor-ring bound from the hardware definitions rather than from Linux defaults.
Declare TX and RX segment limits consistent with the descriptor format actually used.
Declare the number of free lists per RX queue to match the buffer-queue model of the device.
State explicitly which capability flags the driver claims and why.
acceptance_criteria: Every field is traceable to a hardware definition or an explicit design decision recorded in this item.
Ring size bounds accepted by iflib match the device descriptor-count constraints.

work_items.title: ifdi_attach_pre: resource allocation and software context
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: the first half of the Linux probe function
obligations: Map BARs and record bus tag/handle for register access before any device access.
Populate if_softc_ctx_t: queue counts, descriptor counts, capabilities, MSI-X vector count, TX/RX queue sizes.
Complete device reset and capability negotiation before returning, since iflib allocates queues immediately after.
Return a non-zero error rather than leaving the context partially initialised.
acceptance_criteria: A failure at any point unwinds every resource allocated so far.
scctx values reported to iflib match what the hardware negotiation actually granted.

work_items.title: ifdi_attach_post: interface finalisation
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: register_netdev and the netdev feature/ops assignment
obligations: Publish media types and initial media state.
Set the interface capabilities and the enabled subset.
Do not register the ifnet directly; iflib owns interface registration.
acceptance_criteria: ifconfig reports the interface with the expected capability and media lists after attach.

work_items.title: ifdi_detach and teardown ordering
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: pci_driver.remove and unregister_netdev
obligations: Quiesce the device before releasing any resource that the device can still write to.
Drain deferred work and stop all timers before freeing the structures they reference.
Release resources in the exact reverse order of acquisition.
acceptance_criteria: Detach under active traffic does not produce use-after-free or DMA to freed memory.
All busdma tags, maps and interrupt handlers are released.

work_items.title: busdma tag strategy for descriptor rings and buffers
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: dma_alloc_coherent, dma_map_single/dma_map_page and the Linux DMA mask model
obligations: Separate tags for descriptor rings (coherent, aligned) and packet buffers (streaming, segmented).
Set maxsize, nsegments and maxsegsize from the descriptor format, not from arbitrary constants.
State the boundary and alignment constraints that the hardware imposes on each ring.
Record which tags iflib creates on the driver's behalf and which the driver must create itself.
acceptance_criteria: Every DMA allocation names the tag it comes from and the sync operations that guard it.
No allocation relies on physically contiguous memory unless the hardware requires it.

work_items.title: ifdi_tx_queues_alloc and ifdi_rx_queues_alloc
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: driver-private queue allocation performed during Linux open/probe
obligations: Accept the virtual and physical ring addresses that iflib supplies; do not allocate the descriptor rings again.
Attach driver-private queue state to the iflib-provided queue arrays.
Handle the split-queue model of the device explicitly: map each iflib queue index onto the correct hardware queue and buffer queue.
Free everything allocated here, and only that, in ifdi_queues_free.
acceptance_criteria: Queue allocation failure at any index unwinds all previously allocated queues.
The queue index mapping is documented and reversible.

work_items.title: DMA synchronization placement
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: implicit ordering provided by the Linux DMA API plus dma_wmb/dma_rmb
obligations: Name every point where a descriptor or buffer ownership transfer happens and the sync call that guards it.
Pair every PRE sync with the matching POST sync on the same map.
Do not substitute a CPU memory barrier for a busdma sync; they solve different problems.
acceptance_criteria: Every descriptor read after device write is preceded by a POSTREAD sync.
Every descriptor write before a doorbell is followed by a PREWRITE sync.

work_items.title: isc_txd_encap: descriptor construction from if_pkt_info
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ndo_start_xmit and the skb-based TX path
obligations: Consume the pre-loaded DMA segment list from if_pkt_info; do not map the mbuf again.
Translate checksum and TSO requests from the csum flags into the device descriptor fields.
Return the new producer index; iflib owns ring accounting.
Reject a packet with more segments than the descriptor format allows rather than truncating it.
acceptance_criteria: Segment count, offsets and lengths written to descriptors match the supplied segment list exactly.
Checksum and TSO offload requests map to the same hardware behaviour as the source driver.

work_items.title: isc_txd_flush and isc_txd_credits_update
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: netdev doorbell writes and NAPI-driven TX completion cleaning
obligations: Write the tail doorbell only after the descriptor writes are visible to the device.
Report the number of completed descriptors, honouring the clear flag semantics.
Handle the completion-queue model of the device rather than assuming in-place descriptor writeback.
acceptance_criteria: Credits reported never exceed descriptors actually completed by hardware.
A completion sweep is idempotent when called with the clear flag unset.

work_items.title: isc_rxd_available and isc_rxd_pkt_get
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: NAPI poll receive loop building skbs
obligations: Count only descriptors whose done bit is set, bounded by the budget argument.
Fill if_rxd_info with fragment indices and lengths; iflib assembles the mbuf chain.
Translate hardware checksum status into csum flags, reporting only what the hardware verified.
Propagate RSS hash and type so the stack can use hardware flow distribution.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-fragment frames are reported with correct per-fragment lengths and total length.
A malformed or errored descriptor is reported as an error rather than delivered upward.

work_items.title: isc_rxd_refill and isc_rxd_flush
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: driver-managed page/buffer recycling on the Linux RX path
obligations: Post the buffer addresses supplied by iflib into the correct buffer queue for the split-queue model.
Do not allocate receive buffers; iflib owns buffer supply.
Write the buffer-queue tail doorbell only in the flush method.
acceptance_criteria: Refill never posts more buffers than iflib supplied, and never reposts an in-flight buffer.
Buffer-queue and completion-queue indices stay consistent under sustained receive load.

work_items.title: ifdi_msix_intr_assign: vector allocation and queue binding
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: pci_alloc_irq_vectors plus request_irq per queue
obligations: Allocate the admin vector separately from queue vectors.
Bind each RX queue to its own vector and associate TX queues per the device interrupt model.
Program the device interrupt-vector mapping registers to match the iflib assignment.
Name every allocated interrupt so it can be identified in vmstat -i.
acceptance_criteria: The hardware vector map and the iflib assignment agree for every queue.
Partial allocation failure releases all vectors already allocated.

work_items.title: Interrupt enable and disable methods
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: napi_schedule driven masking and per-vector enable/disable writes
obligations: Implement per-queue enable so iflib can rearm a single vector after processing.
Make global disable authoritative: after it returns, the device must not raise any interrupt.
Preserve interrupt-throttling configuration across enable and disable.
acceptance_criteria: No interrupt is delivered after ifdi_intr_disable returns.
Rearming one queue does not disturb the state of any other queue.

work_items.title: Admin interrupt handling and event dispatch
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: Linux threaded IRQ or workqueue-based admin event processing
obligations: Keep the filter routine free of sleeping operations and of control-queue message processing.
Defer mailbox and link-event processing to the admin task.
Rearm the admin cause only after the deferred handler has consumed the event.
acceptance_criteria: No control-queue transaction is executed in filter context.
Admin events are not lost when they arrive while the deferred handler is running.

work_items.title: ifdi_init and ifdi_stop
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ndo_open and ndo_stop
obligations: Bring the device to a fully configured running state in ifdi_init, including queue enable and filter programming.
Make ifdi_stop quiesce hardware queues and stop DMA before returning.
Tolerate being called when already in the requested state.
Do not sleep waiting for a control-queue response longer than the iflib context lock allows; document the wait strategy.
acceptance_criteria: ifconfig up/down cycles repeatedly without leaking queue state or losing link.
After ifdi_stop, hardware performs no further DMA into driver memory.

work_items.title: ifdi_update_admin_status and link state propagation
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: netif_carrier_on/off driven from Linux link event handlers
obligations: Process pending control-queue messages from this callback.
Report link state and baudrate to iflib rather than manipulating the ifnet directly.
Keep the callback bounded in time; it runs on the iflib admin task.
acceptance_criteria: Link transitions observed by hardware appear in ifconfig within one admin poll interval.
Reported baudrate matches the negotiated link speed.

work_items.title: ifdi_multi_set, ifdi_promisc_set and address filtering
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ndo_set_rx_mode and the Linux address list helpers
obligations: Enumerate multicast addresses with the FreeBSD iterator; the Linux list structures do not exist.
Fall back to all-multicast when the hardware filter capacity is exceeded, and record that decision.
Apply promiscuous mode changes through the control plane the device actually requires.
acceptance_criteria: Joining and leaving multicast groups updates the hardware filter.
Exceeding filter capacity degrades to all-multicast rather than dropping addresses silently.

work_items.title: ifdi_mtu_set and frame size constraints
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ndo_change_mtu
obligations: Validate the requested MTU against the hardware maximum frame size before accepting it.
Return EINVAL for an unsupported value instead of clamping it.
Record whether an MTU change requires a queue reinitialisation on this device.
acceptance_criteria: The accepted MTU range matches the hardware capability reported at attach.
Traffic continues correctly across an MTU change at the new frame size.

work_items.title: VLAN registration callbacks
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ndo_vlan_rx_add_vid and ndo_vlan_rx_kill_vid
obligations: Maintain the VLAN filter set across interface down/up cycles.
Claim IFCAP_VLAN_HWFILTER only when the hardware filter is actually programmed.
Handle VLAN tag insertion and stripping consistently with the claimed capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: Configured VLANs survive an ifconfig down/up cycle.
Tagged traffic is filtered exactly as the claimed capability set implies.

work_items.title: ifmedia integration: ifdi_media_status and ifdi_media_change
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ethtool link settings and Linux PHY/link ops
obligations: Map every link speed the device reports onto an IFM_* media type.
Report IFM_AVALID and IFM_ACTIVE truthfully based on the current link state.
Reject unsupported forced-media requests rather than accepting them silently.
acceptance_criteria: ifconfig media reports the actual negotiated speed and duplex.
Every speed advertised by the device has a distinct media entry.

work_items.title: Capability advertisement and offload negotiation
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: netdev features/hw_features and ethtool offload control
obligations: Claim only offloads that the datapath methods actually implement.
Keep the hwassist mask consistent with the enabled capability set at all times.
Handle SIOCSIFCAP transitions, including disabling an offload while traffic is running.
Record for each Linux feature flag whether it maps to a capability, is handled by iflib, or is dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Every claimed capability has a corresponding descriptor-level implementation in the datapath items.
Toggling each capability with ifconfig produces the expected change in offload behaviour.

work_items.title: Control-queue transport on FreeBSD
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: Linux DMA plus completion/wait-queue based mailbox transport
obligations: Allocate mailbox descriptor rings and message buffers through busdma with explicit sync points.
Define the wait strategy for a response: which lock is held, whether the caller may sleep, and the timeout.
Serialize concurrent senders without holding a spin lock across a device round trip.
Preserve the message sequencing and retry semantics of the source transport.
acceptance_criteria: A control message issued from the admin task and one from an ioctl path cannot interleave incorrectly.
A lost or timed-out response is reported as an error and does not wedge the transport.

work_items.title: Asynchronous virtchnl event processing
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: workqueue and delayed_work driven virtchnl event handling
obligations: Run event processing on a context that may sleep, never in filter context.
Drain and stop every task and callout before the structures they touch are freed.
Keep the ordering guarantees the source driver relied on between events and requests.
acceptance_criteria: Detach during an in-flight event completes without use-after-free.
Event ordering matches the source driver for reset, link and configuration events.

work_items.title: Locking model on the target
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: spinlock_t, mutex, rtnl_lock and RCU
obligations: State which iflib-owned lock already covers each datapath and control path, and add a driver lock only where iflib does not.
Map each source lock to a target primitive, or justify its removal.
Declare the lock order and prove it is acyclic.
Replace RCU-protected pointer publication with an explicit target mechanism; do not assume an RCU equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: No sleepable lock is acquired in a context that cannot sleep.
The declared lock order holds on every path, including error paths.

work_items.title: Timers and deferred execution
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: timer_list, delayed_work and workqueues
obligations: Use ifdi_timer for per-queue watchdog work instead of a private periodic timer where iflib already provides one.
Every callout must be initialised with a lock and drained before teardown.
Distinguish work that must not be lost from work that may be coalesced, and pick the primitive accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: No callout or task can run after the structures it references are freed.
Periodic work continues across interface down/up cycles as the source driver did.

work_items.title: Counter reporting through ifdi_get_counter
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: ndo_get_stats64 and ethtool statistics
obligations: Map each standard interface counter to the hardware or software source that backs it.
Let iflib report the counters it already maintains; do not double count.
Expose device-specific counters through the sysctl tree rather than inventing interface counters.
acceptance_criteria: netstat -i counters advance correctly under traffic.
No counter is reported from two sources at once.

work_items.title: sysctl tree for device state and statistics
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: sysfs, debugfs, devlink and ethtool -S
obligations: Anchor the tree under the device node so it is removed automatically at detach.
Expose per-queue statistics under a per-queue subtree.
Never expose a raw kernel pointer or allow an unprivileged write to change device state.
acceptance_criteria: The sysctl subtree disappears completely after detach.
Every statistic previously reachable through ethtool -S has a sysctl equivalent or a recorded decision to drop it.

work_items.title: Loader tunables and driver configuration
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: Linux module parameters and devlink parameters
obligations: Express every source module parameter as a loader tunable or a sysctl, or record that it is dropped.
Mark boot-time-only values read-only after attach.
Validate tunable values at attach and fall back to a documented default on an invalid value.
acceptance_criteria: Each source module parameter is accounted for: mapped, replaced or explicitly dropped.
An out-of-range tunable produces a warning and a safe default rather than an attach failure.

work_items.title: Kernel module build definition
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: Kbuild Makefile and Kconfig
obligations: Produce a bsd.kmod.mk-based Makefile listing only the sources that survive the exclusion pass.
Declare the generated glue sources that FreeBSD requires but Linux does not.
Keep the build free of Linux compatibility headers.
acceptance_criteria: The module builds against a matching /usr/src with no Linux compatibility shim in the include path.
The source list matches the retained-method inventory of this baseline.

work_items.title: Target validation plan
work_items.replaces_source_mechanism: Linux selftests and driver-specific CI
obligations: Define a load/unload cycle test that runs before any hardware attach is attempted.
Define unit-level tests for the descriptor construction and completion paths that run in userspace.
Define a hardware bring-up sequence with an explicit abort condition at each step.
State the console or out-of-band access required before the first attach on real hardware.
acceptance_criteria: Every mandatory work item in this profile has at least one test that exercises it.
The plan states what to do when a step fails, not only what to run.
